title: P0456

definition.text: P0456: EVAP system leak detected (very small leak)
definition.value: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Very Small Leak)
definition.sourceText: P0456: EVAP system leak detected (very small leak)

causes.text: Fuel cap not completely closed after fueling
causes.quote: The concern is most likely the result of the customer not getting the fuel cap completely closed after fueling the vehicle.

causes.text: EVAP leak at vent control valve O-ring
causes.document: Nissan TSB: DTC P0456 caused by EVAP leak at vent control valve O-ring
causes.appliesTo: Applied Nissan vehicles only; bulletin states not caused by loose cap for those vehicles

causes.text: Some P0456 concerns corrected by PCM software update (Stellantis; SLVT required)
EVAP leak at the fuel tank air filter and, when the code is active, the natural vacuum leak detector (NVLD)
causes.document: Kia Service Bulletin 041 (Service Action SA395), 2017-2019 Niro (DE HEV)
causes.appliesTo: 2017-2019 Kia Niro (DE HEV) built Nov 1, 2016 - Mar 22, 2019
causes.quote: This bulletin provides the procedure to perform an evaporative leak test and replace the fuel tank air filter, and, if necessary, the natural vacuum leak detector (NVLD) on some Niro (DE HEV) vehicles, produced from November 1, 2016 through March 22, 2019, which may experience an evaporative leak concern with DTC P0456.

urgency.document: U.S. EPA Fact Sheet EPA 420-F-97-003 (May 1997), Frequently Asked Questions About On-Board Diagnostics
urgency.quote: It is important to note that an illuminated dashboard light, as described here, is intended to inform the driver of the need for service, NOT of the need to stop the vehicle. However, service should be sought as soon as possible.
urgency.text: Steady light: get the car serviced as soon as possible, but this is not a reason to stop driving.
urgency.answers: urgency: service as soon as possible (steady light)

guidancePrimary: universal: EPA 420-F-97-003 p.2 (steady: service ASAP, not need to stop; flashing: reduce speed, service ASAP)

verdict.action: Keep driving; book service and get the fault read
verdict.detail: A steady light means a service item, not a stop-driving condition.

guidance.text: Under certain conditions, the dashboard light will blink or flash. This indicates a rather severe level of engine misfire. When this occurs, the driver should reduce speed and seek service as soon as possible.

verdict.action: Reduce speed and have it serviced as soon as possible
verdict.detail: A flashing light is the severe-misfire case, not the steady-light case below it.

guidance.text: For example, if the gas cap is not properly tightened after refueling, the OBD system can detect the vapor leak that exists from the cap not being completely tightened. If the gas cap is subsequently tightened, the dashboard light should be extinguished within a few days.
guidance.document: U.S. EPA Fact Sheet EPA 420-F-97-003 (May 1997), Frequently Asked Questions About On-Board Diagnostics

guidance.text: If the malfunction indicator lamp comes on while driving First check the following: Is the fuel tank empty? If it is, fill the fuel tank immediately. Is the fuel tank cap loose? If it is, tighten it securely. The light will go off after several driving trips. If the light does not go off even after several trips, contact your Toyota dealer as soon as possible.

guidance.answers: check yourself first (fuel, cap), then dealer as soon as possible

guidance.text: When "Check Fuel Cap" is displayed on the multi-information display: The fuel tank cap may be unfastened or loose. Turn the engine switch off, check the cap and tighten it securely.

hub.note: The smallest leak threshold in the EVAP family — a pinhole, an O-ring, or a cap that was closed but not sealed. Several manufacturers correct P0456 with a powertrain software update, which is why the service-bulletin list matters as much as the parts list.
hub.verdict: Yes — no driveability risk. Small leaks are the slowest to find.
